v4_model_pathology.symptom: ALL 6 mechanisms converge to obstruction=1.000 at 365 days, regardless of intervention
v4_model_pathology.root_cause: The V4 model has ONLY accumulation (formation → accumulation) with NO biological clearance
v4_model_pathology.equation: obstruction += (protein + cell + thrombus) * factor — MONOTONIC, UNBOUNDED
v4_model_pathology.problem: Real biological systems have turnover: thrombus resolves, endothelialization adapts, flow clears deposits
v4_model_pathology.diagnosis: MODEL PATHOLOGY — the model cannot represent a mechanism that succeeds because it has no clearance pathway

missing_biology: THROMBUS RESOLUTION: clots naturally lyze via plasmin/fibrinolysis — V4 model has no lysis term
ENDOTHELIALIZATION: venous boundary endothelializes over weeks-months, creating native anti-thrombogenic surface — V4 ignores this
FLOW CLEARANCE: non-stagnant flow washes away loose deposits — V4 has no flow-dependent clearance
PROTEIN TURNOVER: adsorbed proteins desorb and are replaced (Vroman effect) — V4 has only adsorption
CELL TURNOVER: adhered cells die/detach and are cleared by flow — V4 has only adhesion
COATING REGENERATION: some coatings self-heal or regenerate — V4 has only degradation
SHEAR-DEPENDENT CLEARANCE: higher shear removes deposits — V4 has no shear term
BIOLOGICAL ADAPTATION: the body adapts to implants over months — V4 has no adaptation
part_1_model_audit.conclusion: The V4 model is a PURE ACCUMULATION model. It CANNOT represent biological success because it has no clearance/remodeling/detachment terms. Every mechanism hitting 1.000 is a MODEL ARTIFACT, not a physical ceiling. The model must be revised before any ceiling declaration.

results.title: A non-hydrocephalic goat experimental model to evaluate a ventriculosinus shunt.
results.abstract: The ventriculosinus shunt is a promising treatment for hydrocephalus. Currently, different shunt techniques exist, and it is not clear whether one is preferable. This pilot study reports on a non-hydrocephalic goat model (Saanen breed) that provides opportunities to evaluate and optimize several aspects of the ventriculosinus shunt technique. Analysis of the coagulation properties of 14 goats by a viscoelastic coagulation monitor showed that goats have a hypercoagulable state compared to humans.

results.abstract: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is a rare, ill-understood disease of significant morbidity. key_findings: El-Shafei retrograde ventriculojugular and ventriculosinus shunts — explicitly use venous pressure and geometry
Sinushunt — experimental work examined anti-reflux behavior, found reflux in some devices
Historical venous-shunt literature discusses anti-stagnation, clotting prevention, and venous pressure dynamics
analysis.implications_for_novelty: The eShunt-specific advantage claim ('venous boundary requires reflux prevention that ventricular catheters don't need') is NOT sufficient for novelty. Historical ventriculosinus/ventriculojugular shunts ALSO face venous-boundary reflux and have addressed it. The #5 candidate must be differentiated from these HISTORICAL venous-shunt architectures, not just from ventricular-catheter anti-fouling.
differentiation_required: How does the eShunt anti-fouling + backflow prevention differ from El-Shafei retrograde ventriculojugular?
How does it differ from Sinushunt anti-reflux design?
What does the eShunt do that historical venous shunts could NOT do?
Is the eShunt-specific advantage about the ENDOVASCULAR deployment method, not the venous boundary itself?
